text:
alex: Hey team — Galileo (large fintech) wants a 2-week POC to replace their current vendor API. Main asks: prompt parity, token billing equivalence, and answers to their security questionnaire. They want a smoke by next Tue. Can we run?

maria: I can own the POC runbook and staging. Need: list of Galileo IPs/firewall rules, sample prompts/responses, and acceptance criteria. Who will own the adapter shim?

devon: I’ll take the adapter shim. Plan: small proxy that maps their request/response shapes to our API + a prompt transform layer. Need their canonical examples. Est 3 days to get basic parity tests running.

ben: For staging we’ll need egress IPs and a dedicated VPC or peering. Also confirm streaming behavior — competitor streams chunked tokens; we usually stream token deltas. If they rely on chunk boundaries we can emulate chunked streaming.

sasha: Security Qs I’ll own: SOC2 status, KMS/HSM support, data residency, retention and redaction, pen-test attestation, and mTLS for private connectors. Can we disable request logging for specific routes during their PII smoke tests?

alex: I’ll upload their sample prompts and the questionnaire PDF here. Also they asked about pricing parity — per-token vs per-response. What’s our recommended stance for the POC? Free credits + a sample billing report?

devon: For parity we should run tokenized consumption on a representative sample and present a mapping doc. Offer POC on free credits and provide a usage report with estimated per-request costs. Also run prompt-delta evals (BLEU/semantic similarity + custom rubric).

maria: Draft acceptance criteria suggestion:
- 10 canonical prompts hit >=95% semantic parity by our eval harness
- Response schema matches their downstream parser for all smoke cases
- p95 latency <= 450ms on their average payload in staging
- No critical security blockers in questionnaire responses

ben: Network specifics for staging: provisional egress IPs 52.23.11.22, 54.82.33.44. We’ll create galileo-poc VPC and peer. Also will disable telemetry sampling for the PII run.

deploy-bot: devops: created sandbox cluster galileo-poc-2026, staging creds sent to alex via DM :white_check_mark:

alex: Got the creds, thanks. devon — can you drop a short script for Galileo to run prompt parity locally?

devon: Yep will provide a curl + eval snippet. Example: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_KEY" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1","prompt":"<sample>","stream":false}'
```
Also include a small local eval harness and instructions to anonymize requests.

maria: We should also document fallback routing: if capacity constrained we route to a quantized variant with documented small output diffs. Add that to runbook so Galileo knows expected differences.

sasha: One blocker: Galileo insists on HSM-managed keys (BYOK). BYOK is only supported on Private deployments. Dedicated + BYOK is possible but requires legal/KMS attestation. Need sales to confirm whether they will accept Dedicated+BYOK or require a Private install. Flagging as potential deal blocker.

alex: I’ll confirm with them today. If BYOK is mandatory and Private is required, we’ll escalate to solutions engineering and legal.

devon: Also note tokenizer differences — their tokenization is slightly different. I’ll add a tokenizer mapping and a prompt preprocessor shim to reduce delta. That should cover most semantic mismatches.

alex: Great. I’ll schedule a 30m kickoff with Galileo next Mon and share meeting notes here. Anything else we should capture now?

maria: Send me expected SLA numbers they want (uptime, latency, support hours) so I can prep rollback and routing docs.

sasha: Ask them to provide a list of production endpoints they call and an anonymized sample of ~100 requests for parity testing. Also confirm any regulatory constraints (e.g., EU residency).

alex: Will do — posting meeting invite + attaching their questionnaire and sample prompts. Thanks all.
